 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Jain

On The 11th Of November, 2024
 Writ Petition No. 33854 of 2024
 Ashish Gupta
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Rahul Mishra - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri V.V. Singh - Dy. G.A. for the respondents / State.
 Order

The petitioner is aggrieved by the notification under Section 11 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "Act of 2013") whereby for construction of road in village Kota, Tehsil- Semariya, Distt. Rewa a primary notification has been published.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2 . It is the contention of the petitioner that the notification is for a total area of .880 hectare in the said village and as per the proposed map appended to the said notification, the part of land of the petitioner in survey No. 93 & 94 is going to be affected by acquisition.

It is the case of the petitioner that the social impact assessment report has been dispensed with in the notification under Section 11 wrongfully mentioning that there is consent of the land owner and also further that there had been acquisition of adjoining land in survey No. 95 ad 96 for construction of the road which was never utilized by the State authority for construction of the road and now just NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55462 2 WP-33854-2024 to benefit the encroachers on the said acquired lands in survey No. 95 and 96 a proposal is being made to acquire the lands including the land of the petitioner in survey No. 93 and 94.
3.

It is the case of the petitioner that he has never given any consent for acquisition of his land and the said fact has been erroneously mentioned in the notification under Section 11 and also that since there is already availability of acquired land in survey No. 95 & 96 there is no requirement of the land of the petitioner to be acquired .

4. The petitioner has submitted a detailed objection mentioning all these facts before Collector,
District Rewa as well as before the land acquisition officer.

The copy of said representation /

sentences.text:
As per Section 15 of the Act of 2013 a person interested in land notified under Section 11 is given a right to submit objections in the matter of area and suitability of the proposed acquisition,
justification offered for public purpose and the findings of social impact assessment.

As per Section 15(2) of the Act of 2013 the objection shall be made to the Collector in writing and the Collector is under obligation to decide the objection after giving the objector an opportunity of being heard in person or being represented by an advocate and has to pass a specific order on the objection.
6.

(2) Every objection under sub-section (1) shall be made to the Collector in writing, and the Collector shall give the objector an opportunity of being heard in person or by any person authorised by him in this behalf or by an Advocate and shall, after hearing all such objections and after making such further inquiry, if any, as he thinks necessary, either make a report in respect of the land which has been notified under sub-section (1) of section 11, or make different reports in respect of different parcels of such land, to the appropriate Government, containing his recommendations on the objections, together with the record of the proceedings held by him along with a separate report giving therein the approximate cost of land acquisition, particulars as to the number of affected families likely to be resettled, for the decision of that Government.
(3) The decision of the appropriate Government on the objections made under sub-section (2) shall be final."

7. In the present case, as the petitioner has already submitted a representation before the Collector within the time limit under Section 15, this petition is disposed of directing the respondents No.3 &
4 to decide the objection of the petitioner (Annexure P-10) by strictly adhering the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55462 4 WP-33854-2024 provisions of Section 15 of the Act of 2013 and pass a specific order considering the objections of the petitioner after giving opportunity to the petitioner to represent his case before the authority.
Let needful be done within a period of two months from the date of production of copy of this order.
